note: The auditor agent's ranked list of bugs, data problems and code-quality work (agents/auditor.md).

items.title: ready_count compared timestamps as strings
items.detail: history.ready_count compared ISO strings, wrong if offsets differ (+05:30 vs +00:00). Now parses datetimes.

items.title: variety.py duplicate-topic cutoff compares ISO strings
items.detail: Same string comparison at generator/variety.py:94. Guard blocks the auditor from variety.py; owner to change.

items.title: fact_value showed 9.996 as '9.' and -0.5 as '0.5'
items.detail: Split decimals before rounding, so a value that rounds up lost its digits and kept a trailing dot; int() dropped the sign of values between -1 and 0. Now rounds to 2 places first.

items.title: emi crashed at 0% interest (no-cost EMI)
items.detail: Both the maths kind and the number check's independent formula divided by zero when rate_pct is 0, a real Indian offer and a likely trap-alert story. Now principal / months.

items.title: Zero amounts give bare ZeroDivisionError / math domain error
items.detail: lumpsum/sip/card_min_due with amount 0 (ratio = final/0, nice_axis(0)) fail with an unhelpful message instead of a writer-facing one. Writer error only; validate inputs > 0 in maths.compute. Also (2026-10-24): loan_prepay at 0% interest and income_tax_bands with income 0 divide by zero, in renderer/models/maths.py and generator/numbers.py alike. Unlikely inputs; a clear ValueError would do. Fixed 2026-11-06: maths.compute raises a clear ValueError for amount, monthly or income at or below zero and for loan_prepay at 0%; test in renderer/tests/test_maths.py.

items.title: Event specs {'end': 0} rejected and {'word': -1} means first word
items.detail: _event_time tests spec.get('end') for truthiness, so end 0 raises; negative word indices clamp to 0 rather than counting from the end as a writer would expect.

items.title: check_script and build repeat the per-beat resolve/fill/spoken steps
items.detail: Both compute maths, facts, figures, check beat ids and fill each beat. Extract one _prepare(script) returning results, figures, sources, beats. Deferred: the owner rewrote build.py on 2026-10-17 (3-day rule).

items.title: Watchdog crashed every hour once Scout/Studio reported run times
items.detail: scheduleCheck passed every AgentActivity with start/finish to scheduleOverlap, which looks each id up in SCHEDULE. 'scout' and 'studio' are not there, so entry(id).ist threw a TypeError before any notification was raised or resolved. Since the first timestamped Scout report (2026-10-18) the watchdog did nothing. Now unscheduled runs are skipped (isScheduled).

items.title: Workflow failures are hidden by '| tee' without pipefail
items.detail: data-audit, ingest, market, publish, stats and watchdog run 'npm run x | tee ...' under the default 'bash -e' shell, which has no pipefail, so a crashed job shows green and the watchdog's workflow-failure check never fires. Workflows are owner-only: raised as a notification. Owner added 'shell: bash' (bash -eo pipefail) to every tee step in 1747612 (2026-10-19).

items.title: ingestedAt picked the newest manifest by string order
items.detail: buildRoutineSettings sorted createdAt strings; with mixed UTC offsets the text order isn't time order (same class as gen-001). Now compared as instants (newestStamp). All manifests use +00:00 today, so no wrong value has shipped.

items.title: watchdog.ts computes the IST hour and weekday by hand in two places
items.detail: pipelineChecks and agentChecks repeat the istHour formula, and agentChecks repeats the 330-minute offset for the weekday. One istClock(now) helper next to istDay in lib would remove three copies. Small; for a later night (needs a test first). Fixed 2026-11-11 on agent/auditor/2026-11-11-2: workers/lib/ist-clock.ts istHour/istWeekday, test pins the old formulas against India's clock.

items.title: Video 'Avg viewed' was an unweighted mean of daily %
items.detail: store.db.ts totals() averaged each day's averageViewPercentage equally, so a 10-view day counted as much as the 1,000-view launch day and zero-view days pulled the figure toward 0. The agents' metrics (agents-sync) weight by views, so the dashboard disagreed with what the evaluator sees. Now view-weighted; totals() moved to lib/totals.ts (pure) with workers/tests/dashboard-totals.test.ts.

items.title: listVideos takes 300 rows without an order
items.detail: prisma.video.findMany({take: 300}) has no orderBy, so once there are more than 300 videos Postgres may return any 300 and the newest can vanish from the Videos page. 25 videos today, so not urgent; fix: orderBy createdAt desc before take (needs a DB to test).

items.title: Usable feed topics hidden behind blocked ones
items.detail: topics.for_state showed the first 8 open topics by priority; when they were all in blocked categories, usable ones further down never reached the planner. Usable topics are now listed first. Null expires/found in the feed no longer crash state.

items.title: Mark-uploaded stretches run durations to days
items.detail: The manual_upload AgentRun shares the video id, so the Runs page duration and the Agents page video-run clusters ran from 04:07 to the moment the owner marked it uploaded. Fixed: runEndMs ignores it; getAgents excludes it.

items.title: Analytics Avg viewed counted fresh videos as 0%
items.detail: Videos with only live counters (no Analytics rows yet) entered the channel mean at 0%. Fixed with meanViewPct.

items.title: Week-over-week change biased down
items.detail: Overview and Analytics compare the last 7 days with the 7 before, but Analytics runs 1-2 days behind, so the last days are 0 and flat traffic shows about -20%. Fix: drop trailing days after the latest day with a VideoStat row. Update 2026-10-27: views and likes now fill lagging days from the live counters (estimated days, lib/totals.ts), so the bias is mostly gone for them; subscribers have no live counter and are still biased down. Fixed 2026-11-05: weekOverWeek moved to lib/totals.ts; subscribers leave out trailing estimated days (test workers/tests/dashboard-week-over-week.test.ts). The Analytics page now compares server-side periods and has no such delta.

items.title: Settings row labels click their first button
items.detail: Row renders a <label>; clicking the Upload days text toggles Sun, clicking the Trend slots text adds a slot. Fix: Row as <div> for multi-control rows. The file holds owner-only schedule lines, so the guard may block an agent edit; may need the owner.

items.title: Saving settings can undo a change made elsewhere
items.detail: Save sends the whole form, reverting a proposal approval or pause toggle made from another page while the form had unsaved edits. Fix: send only changed keys. Same guard caveat as dui-004.

items.title: Calendar hides planned slots while uploads are paused
items.detail: Paused is the manual-posting mode, where the slots matter most. Same guard caveat.

items.title: Made today / Daily output count long videos against the Shorts target
items.detail: app/page.tsx counts all video runs; needs the format on Run.

items.title: Overview backlog days mix Shorts and long videos
items.detail: Divides all queued videos by the daily Short slots; should use runway('short') from posting-plan.ts.

items.title: Video page shows global queue number for long videos
items.detail: queue # uses the global queuePosition; the queue page numbers each format separately.

items.title: Videos search box keeps a cleared query
items.detail: q state isn't synced with the URL; navigating to /videos keeps the old text.
items.fixedNote: Already fixed on main: videos/page.tsx syncs q with the URL (useEffect on urlQ). Confirmed 2026-11-10.

items.title: Sign-out unhandled rejection
items.detail: await fetch without catch; on a network error the redirect never runs. try/finally.

items.title: Step timeline copied between Runs and video page
items.detail: app/runs/page.tsx and app/videos/[id]/page.tsx render the same step list; one component.

items.title: IST day helper written five ways
items.detail: istDayOf (slots.ts, posting-plan.ts), istDay (format.ts, store.db.ts), dayFmt (run-times.ts): one helper in format.ts.

items.title: Overview hardcodes the daily target
items.detail: DAILY_TARGET = 3 in app/page.tsx instead of settings; TAB/WEEKDAYS constants duplicated across pages.

items.title: Watchdog counted the owner's dashboard actions as part of a video run
items.detail: workers/watchdog.ts scheduleCheck clustered every AgentRun with a video from the last 30 h. Marking a video uploaded, editing or removing it logs a manual_* step hours later, so the main run looked like it ran from 04:07 to the time of the click, raising a false 'A routine overran its slot' warning. videoSteps() in workers/lib/schedule.ts now drops them (the dashboard's AFTER_RUN list).

items.title: Editing or removing a video stretched its run on the Runs page
items.detail: apps/dashboard/src/lib/run-span.ts AFTER_RUN listed only manual_upload; the newer manual_edit and manual_remove steps (store.db.ts) stretched the run's duration the same way. Added both.

items.title: Cover and frame gates open images without closing them
items.detail: renderer/craft.py frame_problems and cover_problems call Image.open per still without closing. Harmless at today's still counts; worth a `with` if long videos grow their contact sheets. Closed 2026-11-06, not a bug: Pillow closes a file it opened by path once a single-frame image loads, and dhash/empty_share load every still (a ResourceWarning check passes on the old code).

items.title: Mark as uploaded with a corrected link kept the old video's numbers
items.detail: markUploaded (store.db.ts) can be repeated to correct the YouTube link, but unlike updateVideo it kept the Upload's live counters and VideoStat rows. live-stats writes GREATEST(old, new), so a wrong link with more views stayed on the dashboard for good. Now both paths use relinked() (lib/youtube-link.ts) and drop the old counters and stats. Test: workers/tests/dashboard-relink.test.ts.

items.title: Overview 'uploads in 7 days' counted removed videos
items.detail: getOverview's upload count had no deletedAt filter, while every other overview total skips videos the owner removed. Added video: live to the count (a Prisma filter; no DB in unit tests).

items.title: check-plan crashed on a malformed demand or reach reason
items.detail: reach.check_plan compared plan.demand.views with 1,000,000 without checking it is a number ("1.2M" raised TypeError) and called .get on reach_reason and demand without checking they are objects. formats.check_plan already reports those as problems; reach now treats them as missing. Test in generator/tests/test_reach.py.

items.title: Overview 7-day totals take 8 days of Analytics rows
items.detail: getOverview (and store.sample.ts) sum VideoStat days >= today-7, which is 8 calendar days counting today. Today and yesterday are usually empty (Analytics lag), so the effect is small; decide the window together with dui-003 (week-over-week delta) so both use the same 7 days. Fixed 2026-10-29: windowStart(today, 7) in lib/totals.ts (today-6 to today, the same 7 days as the week-over-week chart's last 7 daily rows), used by store.db.ts and store.sample.ts; test workers/tests/dashboard-window.test.ts.

items.title: Mark as uploaded with a future time counts the video as published
items.detail: markUploaded always set status and upload state to published. A Short scheduled in YouTube Studio (private until its time) then counted as published in the dashboard's totals and lists before it went live; data audit 2026-10-26 flagged v-20261026-01 (publishAt 2026-10-27 01:37 UTC, private). Now a linked video with a publish time ahead starts as scheduled, and refreshPublished (stats/publish jobs) promotes it once YouTube shows it public. Test in workers/tests/dashboard-relink.test.ts.

items.title: Live counters never follow YouTube down
items.detail: live-stats.ts wrote GREATEST(stored, fetched), so when YouTube removed invalid views the dashboard kept the old peak for good (audit 27 Oct: v-20261026-03 showed 75 views, YouTube 57). Fixed 2026-10-28: nextLiveCount() in lib/live-counter.ts keeps the larger number only on a small dip (2 or 2%, under the audit's slack) and follows a real drop.

items.title: Skip to end / Upload now kept the owner's pick
items.detail: The queue sorts pickedAt first, then queuePosition. videoAction 'skip' only moved queuePosition, so skipping the picked video left it at the front (toast said 'Moved to the end'); 'upload-now' left pickedAt set too, unlike the publisher. Fixed: lib/queue-actions.ts skipToEnd/uploadNow clear the pick; used by store.db.ts and store.sample.ts; test workers/tests/dashboard-queue-actions.test.ts. Re-shipped 2026-11-04 from commit 16e52ca once the merge check's Playwright was upgraded (dashboard agent, 1.64.1).

items.title: Every ingest re-applies the editor ranking and undoes Skip to end
items.detail: importEditorRanking (workers/lib/agents-sync.ts) runs on every ingest (push + every 6h) with the same ranking.json and sorts unlocked videos by editor rank, so a video the owner skipped returns to its ranked place within hours. Skip doesn't set orderLocked (and locked videos go to the front, so it can't). Needs a design choice: apply a ranking only once per rankedAt (store the last applied rankedAt), or let skip mark the video 'held back' so the ranking keeps it last. Not fixed tonight: changes queue semantics the owner just designed.

items.title: Dragging the picked video does nothing
items.detail: reorderQueue saves the dragged order but the list is read back pick-first, so a picked video snaps back to the top. Either clear the pick when the owner drags it, or block dragging it with a hint.

items.title: Sample store: Mark stale only accepts queued videos
items.detail: store.db.ts allows stale on queued, qa_passed and rendered; store.sample.ts only queued, so the sample dashboard and e2e tests behave differently. Fixed: one rule, lib/queue-actions.ts canMarkStale (STALE_STATUSES), used by both stores; test in workers/tests/dashboard-queue-actions.test.ts.

items.title: downloadReleaseAsset (gh path) hides rename errors as 'gh not found'
items.detail: Without GITHUB_TOKEN it downloads '*.mp4' and picks a file not in the directory before; if the file already existed (re-download with --clobber) it falls back to 'video.mp4', renameSync throws ENOENT, and the ENOENT catch meant for a missing gh binary swallows it, ending in 'no GITHUB_TOKEN and the gh CLI was not found'. A release with two .mp4 assets picks one by readdir order. Local runs only (Actions has a token; publish.ts uses a fresh temp dir), so low.

items.title: Hedge check counted "can't" as the hedge "can"
items.detail: generator/story.py HEDGES used \bcan\b, which matches the "can" in "can't" / "can’t" (the apostrophe is a word boundary), so confident lines ("You can't sell it") counted toward MAX_HEDGES 2 and could fail a script and use up its rewrites. Fixed 2026-11-03: can(?!['’]t). Test test_cant_is_certain_not_a_hedge. Open question left as is: "May" the month also counts as a hedge (true-history dates).

items.title: A malformed maths `facts` link crashed number-check
items.detail: topics.check_fact_inputs called .items() on maths[].facts and float() on the fact's value, outside number_check's ValueError guard: `"facts": [1]` (a list) raised AttributeError and a fact without a numeric value raised KeyError/TypeError, a traceback instead of a note the writer can fix. Fixed 2026-11-03: both come back as notes. Test test_a_malformed_fact_link_is_a_note_not_a_crash.

items.title: Video page 'typical' retention curve used 10 arbitrary peers
items.detail: getVideoStudio averaged the curves of peers.slice(0, 10), but loadVideos has no orderBy, so the 'typical' curve on a video's Analytics tab came from whichever 10 published videos Postgres returned first (old Shorts of a different length and story), not the last 10 as the overview card does. Fixed: studio-calc latest() (newest first by publishAt), used for the typical curve, the typical first-48-hours line and the overview's recent curves. Test workers/tests/dashboard-studio-calc.test.ts.

items.title: 48-hour views mix IST publish days with YouTube's Pacific-time days
items.detail: contentRow's views48 sums VideoStat days from the IST publish date to the next day, but YouTube Analytics days are Pacific time. A 12:37 IST Short goes out at 23:07 PST the day before, so its first ~1 h is left out and the window runs ~49 h. Small and consistent across videos, so benchmarks are still fair; fix only together with the other 48 h figures (metrics/videos.json views48h) so they agree.

items.title: Hourly snapshots skip a Short until stats marks it published
items.detail: workers/snapshot.ts only reads uploads with state 'published'; a scheduled Short becomes 'published' when stats.ts (every 3 h) sees it public, so the first 1–3 hours have no snapshot and the video page's first-48-hours chart spreads those views evenly from publish time. Option: also snapshot 'scheduled' uploads whose publishAt has passed.

items.title: A green stats run with a passing failure never moves statsRefreshedAt
items.detail: Since 4 Nov (owner) a single passing YouTube error leaves the Stats job green, but statsRefreshedAt was only written when nothing failed, so the Analytics page's 'updated' time froze and the data audit would report stats_stale after 48 h while every run was green. Now written unless the failure is serious (statsOutcome in workers/lib/stats-failures.ts).

items.title: Nothing checks the script carries the plan's arms
items.detail: story.script_problems / timeline_problems check the variant system's style (shot vs board) and length band from script.arms, but only the writer prompt asks for the copy. A script without arms (or with different ones) skipped both checks silently, so a 'board' test could ship as shot beats or a 20-27 s assignment run 34 s. run_number_check now fails when script.arms != plan.arms, like script.shape. Test in generator/tests/test_run.py.

items.title: A budget-test plan could tell a big-money story
items.detail: formats.mix_problems let any plan with arms.topic 'budget' through, including one whose story is a core (big-money) format; improvement/arms.py then credits that video's views to the budget option (it reads plan.arms). Dormant while 'budget' is dropped. Now a problem; test in generator/tests/test_shapes.py.

items.title: Variant system labels pre-arms auto uploads as category 27
items.detail: improvement/arms.py infer(): category = '22' if manual else '27'. But workers/lib/youtube.ts categoryOf uploads a video without style.arms as UPLOAD_CATEGORY '22'. Every ready Short made before 4 Nov (no plan.arms) that the API publishes from 5 Nov (the category dimension's since) is counted as option '27' while it went out as 22, so the category test compares 22 with 22. Owner-only file (guard): raised as notification arms-category-label. Fixed by the owner in 9dfe9c2 (2026-11-04): infer() counts a non-manual upload without plan arms as 22.

items.title: 48-hour live views (views48hLive) almost never filled
items.detail: viewsAt48h only took a snapshot 48-51 h after publishing, but the 'hourly' watchdog runs every 5-9 h on GitHub's schedule (4-5 Nov: 09:04, 17:10, 22:36, 03:28, 12:14 UTC), so 0 of 42 videos in metrics/videos.json had views48hLive and the variant system fell back to Analytics' lagging views48h. Now: the exact 48-51 h snapshot when there is one, else a straight line between the snapshots either side of 48 h when at most 12 h apart. The snapshot query's silent catch now logs a warning. Test workers/tests/views-at-48h.test.ts.

items.title: Analytics page 48-hour views counted the publish day alone before Analytics had day two
items.detail: studio.db.ts contentRow summed whatever VideoStat days existed in the first two IST days once a video was 2 days old. Analytics lags 2-3 days, so a new Short often had only its publish day and showed a partial 48-hour figure that benchmarked as a miss, while metrics/videos.json (agents-sync.ts) waits for day two. Now one pure function views48Of in studio-calc.ts waits for the second day too. Test workers/tests/dashboard-views48.test.ts.

items.title: Editor counts an expired trend as fresh until 05:30 IST
items.detail: editor.score compared manifest priority.until (an IST day, as ingest reads it) with the UTC date. The editor runs at 04:07 IST, still the previous UTC day, so a trend that expired yesterday kept +1.0 'fresh' and ranked above better videos. Now compared with the IST day. Also removed stale 45-70 s / 400-600 s length fallbacks (load() always supplies the settings).

items.title: Bad years or rates in a script's maths crash the number check
items.detail: maths.compute let years 0, negative or fractional (2.5, 10.0) and inflation_pct -100 through, so sip/sip_stepup/emi raised a bare ZeroDivisionError and sip/lumpsum/real_return/price_rise/fee_take a TypeError from range(). check_script and number_check only catch ValueError, so `generator.run number-check` stopped with a traceback instead of a note the writer can fix. Now checked up front: a whole number of years >= 1 (an emi: at least one month), rate_pct and inflation_pct above -100. All 69 committed scripts still compute.

items.title: A handed owner note never counts as answered when the agent it was handed to answers 'partly'
items.detail: ackState (workers/lib/agents-sync.ts) only counted an agent as done with a handed note if it closed it, so 'auditor partly -> improver, improver partly -> studio' showed 'waiting for improver' on the dashboard forever, and generator.feedback listed the note to the improver every run. Now an agent has answered once it closed the note or handed it on to anyone but the agent that handed it to it (a handoff straight back still counts as owed). Same rule in Python (has_answered) and TS (hasAnswered); tests in both fail on the old code.

items.title: Growth page crashed on a full timestamp
items.detail: fmtDayKey appended T00:00:00Z to any string; a writtenAt/startedAt/updatedAt written as a full ISO timestamp became an Invalid Date and Intl.format threw RangeError, blanking the page (no error boundary). Fixed: day keys and timestamps both read, unreadable text returned as is.

items.title: Feedback page hid open notes older than 2 days
items.detail: The 'latest only' filter applied to open notes too: an unanswered 3-day-old note, a note an agent answered 'partly' (addressedAt null) and a reopened note all vanished. Fixed: every open note shows; answered ones for 2 days.

items.title: Growth page verdict due date one day early
items.detail: IST midnight plus maxDays printed as a UTC day: a test starting 13 Nov with 7 days showed 'due by 19 Nov' instead of 20 Nov. Fixed with calendar arithmetic on the day key.

items.title: 'Starts today' shown for a test starting tomorrow; 50% confidence shown with no data
items.detail: Negative days printed 'Starts today'; the evaluator's 0.5 placeholder was shown as a real 50% on the overview and Growth page. Fixed.

items.title: Growth page reference Shorts counted only Analytics views
items.detail: Views summed VideoStat only (Analytics lags 2-3 days), lower than every other page; now max(Analytics, live counter) like store.db.ts.

items.title: Watchdog closed daily-job failure notices while still failing
items.detail: It read the 60 newest runs on main; with Publish every 20 min that is ~12 h, so a Data audit or Market failure dropped out and resolveOthers closed its notice. Now each workflow's own latest run is asked; a failed lookup resolves nothing.

items.title: Analytics never fetched a Short's first Pacific-time day
items.detail: stats.ts and stats-deep.ts started queries at the IST publish day; YouTube's days are Pacific, so the 07:07 IST Short's first ~6 h (12:37: ~1 h) were never fetched (views, engaged views, breakdowns). Now the Pacific publish day. Related open item dd-011 (48 h windows).

items.title: A trend Short lost its front-of-queue place in the same ingest
items.detail: importEditorRanking sorted unranked videos last; the 11:30 trend run writes no ranking, so the trend Short ingest put first went behind the morning's ranked Shorts. Urgent (style.source.urgent) videos now sort first after the owner's own order.

items.title: Watchdog queue checks counted long videos as Shorts
items.detail: queue-empty never fired and slot-missed blamed Publish when only a long video was queued (backlogByFormat short 0, long 1 on 12 Nov). Now the Short count. No unit test: the checks live inside a prisma function.

items.title: One invalid Setting row resets every setting to its default
items.detail: loadSettings safeParses the merged object and falls back to DEFAULT_SETTINGS wholesale (comment says bad rows are ignored): a hand-edited row could unpause uploads. Protected file (workers/lib/settings.ts): owner notified.

items.title: A failed breakdown query deletes that breakdown's stored rows
items.detail: stats-deep saveBreakdowns deleteMany({scope}) after fetchScope drops failed kinds; delete only the kinds that succeeded.

items.title: Failed manifests stored as format short
items.detail: ingest.ts creates failed videos without format, so failed long videos count as Shorts; set from the id prefix.

items.title: Two activity reports on one day overwrite each other
items.detail: agents-sync keys activity rows by day-agent from the content, not the file name; a second run's report (2026-11-03-2-dashboard.json) never shows.

items.title: Percent and points formatting written twice
items.detail: growth/page.tsx and page.tsx each define pct and '+x.x pts' with different decimals.
